subject: NorthPeak: post-call technical recap + routing/policy roadmap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@northpeak.ai>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NorthPeak: post-call technical recap + routing/policy roadmap

Elena — thanks again for a productive call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the integration/architecture items we discussed.

High-level notes from today's discovery:
- Primary workload: customer-facing insights API (~120 TPS peak, 20ms median token latency target for short prompts).
- Key features: structured tool-calling for data lookups, embeddings for semantic search, reranker for top-K results, and deterministic fallback to smaller models when latency spikes.
- Security: needs SOC2 evidence and VPC deployment option for production.

Technical items and recommendations (first pass):
1) SDK & auth
   - Use Redwood SDK for streaming responses and function/tool-calling. We recommend API keys scoped per-environment; for prod we suggest short-lived tokens via your KMS + our token exchange.
2) Model routing & latency/cost policy
   - Primary: long-form generation on rwd-4-hip (high cost, quality).
   - Fast path: rwd-4-quant (lower cost, lower context) for <256 tokens.
   - Fallback chain: rwd-4-hip -> rwd-4-quant -> rwd-3-small. Policy: route by predicted token count + real-time P90 latency SLOs.
3) Embeddings & reranker
   - Host embeddings on dedicated pool for consistent throughput; run reranker as a cheap encoder + cross-encoder on dedicated capacity for top-10 re-rank.
4) Structured output / tool calling
   - Use function-calling with validated JSON schema; we’ll provide example schemas and the SDK helper for validation and retries.

Attachments: architecture diagram and a draft routing-policy template attached. Please review and flag anything we missed.

Next steps (proposed):
- Technical deep-dive with Dev (30–45m) to review auth flow + SDK integration (target: next week).
- Provide sample data (anonymized) and a two-week pilot window on a dedicated sandbox pool.
- Deliver policy YAML for your infra team to review.

If that looks good I’ll send calendar invites and drop the Drive + HubSpot links.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
[Attachment: northpeak-arch-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@northpeak.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northpeak.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NorthPeak: post-call technical recap + routing/policy roadmap

Jordan, thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) Latency SLOs: our product team insists on 95th percentile API latency <120ms for short queries (under 256 tokens). Is the fast path you mentioned able to meet that under normal load? Can you share any P95 numbers from similar customers?

2) SOC2: can you outline what evidence you can provide during our procurement review? We’ll need details on audit logs and key rotation.

3) Pilot timeline: we can share anonymized sample payloads by Friday. For the pilot pool, do you support region pinning (US-EAST) and private VPC peering?

If Dev is available Thursday morning our infra engineer can join the deep-dive.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
VP Product, NorthPeak Analytics
elena.ruiz@northpeak.ai | +1 202-555-0147

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@northpeak.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NorthPeak: post-call technical recap + routing/policy roadmap

Elena — quick responses and a tangible starter config.

1) Latency numbers
   - Fast path (rwd-4-quant) P95 observed: ~85–110ms for 128-token median prompts on a 4-GPU dedicated pool (US-EAST, isolated). We’ll instrument a pilot to show exact numbers against your sample payloads.
2) SOC2 evidence
   - We can provide: SOC2 Type II report redacted, audit-log export (API-level), KMS key rotation policy notes, and our SOC contact for an evidence package. If you need an exec NDA first we can route that.
3) Region/VPC
   - We support region pinning (US-EAST) and VPC peering for Redwood Private. For the sandbox pilot we can provide a VPC-isolated sandbox or a dedicated host pool depending on network requirements.

Draft routing-policy (attached):
# routing-policy-template.yaml
# simple policy: route by predicted_tokens then by real-time latency
primary_model: rwd-4-hip
fast_path: rwd-4-quant
fallbacks:
  - rwd-4-quant
  - rwd-3-small
latency_slo_ms: 120
route_by: 
  - predicted_tokens: 
      threshold: 256
      prefer: fast_path
  - realtime_p95_latency: 
      threshold_ms: 120
      action: fallback

I’ll attach the YAML to the Drive. For the function-calling patterns we recommend a strict JSON schema; I’ve included an example schema in the Drive folder as well.

Proposed times for the technical session: Thu 07:30–08:15 PT or Thu 10:00–10:45 PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send an invite with agenda.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
[Attachment: routing-policy-template.yaml]
